heroLead: Greens Landing sits along the Susquehanna River in Bradford County, one of the counties that saw the earliest and heaviest dry-gas Marcellus drilling in the state.
intro: Greens Landing is a small riverside community in Bradford County, near Wysox and Towanda along the Susquehanna. Bradford County was one of the very first areas in Pennsylvania to see large-scale Marcellus horizontal drilling, with Chesapeake Energy historically among the most active operators here, and that early, dense development means real production history for most tracts.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Greens Landing, whether producing, leased and quiet, or a fractional share inherited from riverside or upland family land.

sections.heading: Bradford County's early role in the Marcellus boom
paragraphs: This county was ground zero for a lot of the earliest Marcellus horizontal drilling activity in Pennsylvania, meaning wells here are generally further along in their production life than in counties developed more recently.

sections.heading: River-bottom versus upland tracts near Greens Landing
paragraphs: Land along the Susquehanna here has a different deed history than the upland farm tracts further from the river, driven by decades of flooding, rail, and river-commerce transactions layered on top of the mineral rights themselves.

sections.heading: What we look at before making an offer
paragraphs: We review lease terms, well performance trend, and the specific chain of title for your parcel before naming a number.
Bradford County's Recorder of Deeds in Towanda is where we typically start any title review for this area.

faqs.question: Which operator has been most active in Bradford County near Greens Landing?
faqs.answer: Chesapeake Energy was historically among the most active operators in Bradford County's early Marcellus development, though ownership of specific wells and leases can change hands over time.

faqs.question: Does river-bottom land near Greens Landing have different mineral history than upland tracts?
faqs.answer: It can, given decades of flooding and river-commerce transactions that shaped ownership along the Susquehanna differently than inland farmland — we check the specific chain of title for your parcel.

faqs.question: Are Bradford County wells generally older than in other parts of the play?
faqs.answer: Many are, since this county saw some of the earliest large-scale horizontal drilling in the state, which means wells here are often further along their decline curve.

faqs.question: Is flood history along the Susquehanna near Greens Landing a concern for mineral rights value?
faqs.answer: Flooding affects surface use and structures, not the underlying mineral estate, which exists independently of what happens on the surface above it, so it isn't typically a factor in valuing the interest itself.
